title: fix(objectql): a unique refusal's user-facing sentence names the object and field by label
body:
Fixes #24951

Clause-②: no (text only: the user-facing sentence names the object and field by label, and `developerMessage` opens with the API names; no code, status, outcome or export moves)

## What changed

A unique refusal's user-facing sentence (`DuplicateRecordError.message`) now names the object and the field by their declared `label`. Every door keeps that message as thrown, so a refused record save and a screen flow both show it to the end user.

- Before: `Duplicate record refused on 'crm_account': a unique constraint on 'name' already holds this value. No record was written.`
- After: `Duplicate record refused on 'Account': a unique constraint on 'Account Name' already holds this value. No record was written.`
- Where no label is declared, the sentence uses the API name, so it is byte-identical to before.
- The opening `Duplicate record refused on '` and the closing `No record was written.` do not move. The sentence still starts with `Duplicate`, not with a SQL verb, so the importer's `sanitizeRowError` backstop leaves it alone.

**Where the labels come from.** `DuplicateRecordError` is built in one place, `envelopeUniqueViolation`. It is called from five sites in `engine.ts`, all inside engine methods with the registry in reach:

- the single-row insert door and its retry (`createWithAutonumberResync`);
- the batch insert door;
- update by id;
- update by predicate (`updateMany`).

Each site now passes `this.getSchema(object)`. `envelopeUniqueViolation` is module-internal (it is not in the package's `index.ts`), so its new third argument is not a public signature change. The labels reach the class through one **optional fourth constructor argument**, `{ object?, field? }`. Callers that pass three arguments, including every test and fake in other packages, get the API-name sentence. No new export.

**Diagnostics keep the API names.** `object` and `field` still carry them. `developerMessage` now opens with them: `Duplicate record refused on object 'crm_account', field 'name'. The driver refused …`. Before this PR, `developerMessage` named neither (see Deviations).

**Not moved:** the codes (`DUPLICATE_RECORD` in the engine, `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` on every wire route), the 409 status and the outcome.

## Census, read before the edit

- **Label reach:** all five `envelopeUniqueViolation` call sites are listed above. There is no upsert or bulk site in `packages/objectql` beyond these. `new DuplicateRecordError` appears in source only inside `envelopeUniqueViolation`; every other occurrence is a test.
- **Pins of the sentence** (`git grep` on both phrases across every package, `qa/`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`, `content/docs/`; CHANGELOGs excluded):
  - **Exact-sentence pins on unlabelled fixtures. They stay green because of the fallback:**
    - `rest`: `rest-duplicate-record-arm.test.ts`, `error-response-structured-arm-door-parity.test.ts`;
    - `mcp`: `mcp-unique-violation-wire-code.test.ts`;
    - `plugin-hono-server`: `handler-throw-declared-envelope.test.ts`;
    - `metadata-protocol`: `protocol.batch-row-http-status.test.ts`;
    - `runtime`: `batch-row-driver-text-real-driver.integration.test.ts`.
  - **Stable-part pins:** `runtime`'s `seed-loader-driver-text-real-driver.integration.test.ts` (`dt_acct`, unlabelled) stayed green.
  - **One pin turned red, on a real engine with a labelled object:** `cli`'s `meta-stored-legacy-organization.integration.test.ts` matched `/Duplicate record refused on 'sys_metadata'/`, and `sys_metadata` is labelled `System Metadata`. It moved (see below).
  - **Doc mentions:** `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json` described the sentence with an API name. Both are updated.
  - **A second producer, not touched:** `driver-sql`'s `refuseUpsertConflictOutsideWrittenOrganization` (`sql-driver.ts`) builds a copy of the same sentence with the object's API name. It has no registry and is outside this card's fence (see Acceptance notes).

## Moved pins and docs, by lane

- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta-stored-legacy-organization.integration.test.ts` (**`domain:cli`**). The pin now matches the stable opening `^Duplicate record refused on '` and asserts `error.object === 'sys_metadata'`, so it no longer restates the label.
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` (**`domain:devx`**). The example reads `'Account'` (the object's label).
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json` (**`domain:devx`**). The `qa_unique` clause now says the sentence names the object by its declared label, and by its API name only where none is declared. The item `records-forms.field-unique-enforcement` moves from revision 8 to 9, with one `history` row (ref `#25021`), as the ledger rule asks of a clause change (`domain:devx`, 6305842305).

- **New pins:** `packages/objectql/src/engine-duplicate-record-label-sentence.test.ts`. They drive the real write doors (single insert, batch insert, update by id, update by predicate) on a registry double:
  - the label sentence for a labelled object and field;
  - the API-name fallback for an unlabelled one;
  - the field-less variant (the dialect named only an index);
  - `developerMessage` naming the API names.

  Result: 17/17 passed.
- **Ablation:** I reverted `duplicate-record-error.ts` and `engine.ts` to the base. The marker counts went from 2/5 to 0/0. **13 failed, 4 passed.** The 4 that passed are the fallback pins, which describe the old behaviour. I then restored both files with `git checkout HEAD --`. Each file's blob hash equals the one at `HEAD` (`8830e86e…`, `247b9130…`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the re-run passed 17/17.
- **`@objectstack/objectql`:** `typecheck` exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck` over the new file. Full `test` exit 0: 452 files, 8524 tests.
- **Dependent full suites, each exit 0:**
  - `rest`: 307 files;
  - `runtime`: 432 files;
  - `mcp`: 40 files;
  - `plugin-hono-server`: 35 files;
  - `metadata-protocol`: 251 files, 3 skipped;
  - `service-automation`: 197 files, 2605 tests.

  - `--project unit`: 315 files green. Two files first failed only because `packages/cli` had not been built; they passed after the build.
  - `--project integration`: 165 files green and 1 skipped. Twelve files first failed only for the same build prerequisite and passed after the build. The moved pin passes 7/7.

- **Gates:** I ran every command printed by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `697e25ef6` (104 commands).
  - 101 exited 0 on the first run.
  - 3 exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: unbuilt packages): `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n-coverage`. After a full `turbo run build`, all three exited 0.

## Deviations

- `developerMessage` gained an opening clause naming the API names. The card and the dispatch say it "keeps" them, but on `main` it named neither the object nor the field. Without that clause, the API names would only be on `object` and `field` once `message` uses labels. The seat re-declared the claim's `Clause-②` line in 6305353681 (fix round 1), and the changeset and this body carry the re-declared line.
- `DuplicateRecordError`'s constructor takes an optional trailing argument (`labels`). The class is exported, so this is an additive, optional signature widening. No export was added.

## Acceptance notes

- `driver-sql`'s upsert refusal outside the written organization (`refuseUpsertConflictOutsideWrittenOrganization`) still names the object by API name. It is a driver-side copy of the sentence and has no registry in reach. No engine write door calls `driver.upsert`: its callers, such as the lifecycle service's `cold.upsert`, a seed or a connector, receive the error exactly as the driver throws it. So its text is unchanged here. No carrier.
- On the REST data routes, the wire `developerMessage` is the engine's `message`, so it now names labels. The body's `object` and `field` keys still carry the API names, and the curated `error` text is unchanged.
- The sentence stays English. A localized entry would go in `packages/spec`'s operation-message catalog (`domain:spec`) and is not part of this PR.
